Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] External MS Teams chat invite from IT-impersonating unmanaged or federated tenant · [LLM] Activity involving ommicrosoft.com Cloaked-Ursa Teams typosquat · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender · Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] MFA approval within minutes of inbound external Microsoft Teams chat · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
External MS Teams chat invite from IT-impersonating unmanaged or federated tenant AIDelivery Medium
Hunts for inbound Microsoft Teams chat invitations from external/guest users whose display name or sender domain impersonates internal IT/helpdesk/MSP functions — the exact technique Cloaked Ursa and UNC6692 used to initiate the social-engineering conversation before requesting MFA approval. Rationale: Maps to the article's central narrative — external Teams chat from an unmanaged/federated tenant whose sender display name impersonates IT/helpdesk/MSP. Combines the external-user predicate (#EXT#/onmicrosoft.com/UserType=Guest) with the IT-impersonation lexicon Unit 42 calls out as the lowered-suspicion lure.
ATT&CKT1566.003 T1656
Data sourcesAuthentication Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate inbound chat from a contracted MSP whose display name genuinely includes 'IT Support'
  • Vendor partners pinged via cross-tenant federation for break/fix conversations
  • Internal IT delegate accounts that are mailbox-shared with external collaborators
  • Sales reps from security/IT vendors initiating prospecting chats
  • Conference / training organizers whose tenant names contain 'IT'
Suppression filter
| where UserId !endswith "@your-trusted-msp.com" and UserId !endswith "@your-contracted-vendor.com"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pivot on UserId (sender), ClientIP, and UserAgent — check whether the sender tenant is on your federation Allow list and whether the sender domain typosquats your IT/MSP brand. Look up the recipient's recent chat/MFA history. 2) Contain: if confirmed external impersonation, remove the recipient's MFA-pending session, force token revocation (`Revoke-MgUserSignInSession`), and add the sender tenant or domain to the Teams external-domain Block list; if widespread, restrict Teams federation to allow-list mode (Figure 3 of the article). 3) Hunt: pivot on sender IP to find other recipients hit by the same external tenant; check SigninLogs for MFA prompts to those recipients in the 30 min window after each chat; check CloudAppEvents for any file/URL shared in the chat body.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application =~ "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType in~ ("ChatCreated","MessageSent","MemberAdded","ChatRetrieved","MeetingDetailMessaged")
| extend RawStr = tostring(RawEventData), ActObjStr = tostring(ActivityObjects)
| where AccountType in~ ("Guest","External") or RawStr has_any ("#EXT#","onmicrosoft.com")
| where ActObjStr has_any ("IT Support","IT Department","Help Desk","Helpdesk","Service Desk","IT Admin","Security Team","SOC Team","Managed Service","MSP")
| project Timestamp, ActionType, AccountDisplayName, AccountId, AccountType, IPAddress, CountryCode, UserAgent, ObjectName, ActivityObjects, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload =~ "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("ChatCreated","MessageSent","MemberAdded","MemberRoleChanged")
| extend ParamsStr = tostring(Parameters)
| where UserType in ("Guest","External") or UserId has_any ("#EXT#","#ext#","onmicrosoft.com")
| where ParamsStr has_any ("IT Support","IT Department","Help Desk","Helpdesk","Service Desk","IT Admin","Security Team","SOC Team","Managed Service","MSP")
| project TimeGenerated, Operation, UserId, UserType, ClientIP, UserAgent, OfficeObjectId, ParamsStr
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(office365 OR azure.activeDirectory) (@Workload:MicrosoftTeams OR @evt.name:("ChatCreated" OR "MessageSent" OR "MemberAdded")) (@UserType:(Guest OR External) OR @UserId:(*#EXT#* OR *onmicrosoft.com*)) ("IT Support" OR "IT Department" OR "Help Desk" OR Helpdesk OR "Service Desk" OR "Security Team" OR "Managed Service" OR MSP)
APPLICATION
`cim_Authentication_indexes` sourcetype IN ("o365:management:activity","ms:o365:management") Workload="MicrosoftTeams" Operation IN ("ChatCreated","MessageSent","MemberAdded","MemberRoleChanged") 
| spath input=Parameters 
| eval is_external=if(match(UserId,"(?i)#EXT#|onmicrosoft\.com") OR UserType IN ("Guest","External"),1,0) 
| where is_external=1 
| eval impersonation=if(match(_raw,"(?i)(IT\s?Support|Help\s?Desk|Helpdesk|Service\s?Desk|IT\s?Department|IT\s?Admin|MSP|Managed\s?Service|Security\s?Team|SOC\s?Team)"),1,0) 
| where impersonation=1 
| table _time UserId UserType ClientIP UserAgent Operation OfficeWorkload Parameters 
| sort - _time
MFA approval within minutes of inbound external Microsoft Teams chat AIExploitation High
Correlates an inbound external Teams chat to a user with a successful MFA-satisfied sign-in by that same user inside a 30-minute window. Surfaces the Cloaked Ursa / UNC6692 pattern where the 'IT technician' chat is immediately followed by a victim-approved MFA push. Rationale: 30-minute window pairing an inbound external Teams chat with an MFA-satisfied sign-in by the same recipient maps directly to the article's narrative — 'IT technician' chat → 'approve this MFA' → compromise. Time-window correlation is the noise-killer the BluRaven kb prescribes for this scenario.
ATT&CKT1621 T1566.003
Data sourcesAuthentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate MSP help desk genuinely fixing a sign-in issue with a real user
  • Internal IT walking a user through SSO enrollment via a federated tenant
  • Vendor support chats where a user simultaneously re-authenticates to the same vendor portal
  • Conference Wi-Fi MFA prompt happening to fire during an unrelated external chat
  • Newly-onboarded user receiving both a welcome chat from an external HR consultant AND completing initial MFA setup
Suppression filter
| where SenderUpn !endswith "@your-trusted-msp.com"
Response runbook
1) Triage: open the chat sender's UserId — verify whether the sender tenant is on the Teams federation Allow list. Pull the SigninLogs MFA detail (was it push, SMS, OAuth code, FIDO2?) and the destination IP / country. 2) Contain: if the IP geo, ASN, or device fingerprint of the MFA-approved sign-in doesn't match the victim's baseline, revoke sessions immediately (`Revoke-MgUserSignInSession`), force credential reset, and block the sender tenant in Teams external-access settings. 3) Hunt: pivot on the MFA-success IP for the next 24 hours across SigninLogs — likely the same IP is harvesting other accounts the attacker chatted; also check OfficeActivity MailItemsAccessed, InboxRuleCreated, and CloudAppEvents OAuth grants under the compromised UPN.
let WindowMinutes = 30m;
let ExternalChats = CloudAppEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where Application =~ "Microsoft Teams"
    | where ActionType in~ ("ChatCreated","MessageSent","MemberAdded")
    | extend RawStr = tostring(RawEventData)
    | where AccountType in~ ("Guest","External") or RawStr has_any ("#EXT#","onmicrosoft.com")
    | extend Recipient = tostring(parse_json(tostring(ActivityObjects))[0].Name)
    | project ChatTime = Timestamp, SenderUpn = AccountDisplayName, SenderIP = IPAddress, Recipient, ActionType;
AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ErrorCode == 0
| where AuthenticationRequirement =~ "multiFactorAuthentication"
| extend AuthDetailStr = tostring(AuthenticationDetails)
| where AuthDetailStr has_any ("Mobile app notification","PhoneAppNotification","OAuth Verify","Authenticator App")
| join kind=inner ExternalChats on $left.AccountUpn == $right.Recipient
| where Timestamp between (ChatTime .. ChatTime + WindowMinutes)
| extend DelayMinutes = datetime_diff('minute', Timestamp, ChatTime)
| project ChatTime, MfaApprovalTime = Timestamp, DelayMinutes, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Country, City, Application, RiskLevelDuringSignIn, ConditionalAccessStatus, SenderUpn, SenderIP
| order by MfaApprovalTime desc
let WindowMinutes = 30m;
let ExternalChats = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where OfficeWorkload =~ "MicrosoftTeams"
    | where Operation in~ ("ChatCreated","MessageSent","MemberAdded")
    | where UserType in ("Guest","External") or UserId has_any ("#EXT#","#ext#","onmicrosoft.com")
    | extend ParamsStr = tostring(Parameters)
    | extend Recipient = extract(@"(?i)([A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})", 1, ParamsStr)
    | project ChatTime = TimeGenerated, SenderUpn = UserId, SenderIP = ClientIP, Recipient;
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ResultType == 0
| where AuthenticationRequirement =~ "multiFactorAuthentication"
| extend AuthMethods = tostring(AuthenticationMethodsUsed)
| where AuthMethods has_any ("Mobile app notification","PhoneAppNotification","Microsoft Authenticator")
| join kind=inner ExternalChats on $left.UserPrincipalName == $right.Recipient
| where TimeGenerated between (ChatTime .. ChatTime + WindowMinutes)
| extend DelayMinutes = datetime_diff('minute', TimeGenerated, ChatTime)
| project ChatTime, MfaApprovalTime = TimeGenerated, DelayMinutes, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, Location, AppDisplayName, RiskLevelDuringSignIn, ConditionalAccessStatus, SenderUpn, SenderIP
| order by MfaApprovalTime desc
source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:"Sign-in activity" @properties.status.errorCode:0 @properties.authenticationRequirement:multiFactorAuthentication (@properties.authenticationMethodsUsed:("Mobile app notification" OR "PhoneAppNotification" OR "Microsoft Authenticator"))
#event_simpleName=IdpAuthenticationLog

| AuthenticationRequirement=/multiFactor/i
| Status=/success/i
| AuthenticationMethod=/(Mobile app notification|PhoneAppNotification|Microsoft Authenticator)/i
| groupBy([UserPrincipalName, IPAddress], function=count())

Activity involving ommicrosoft.com Cloaked-Ursa Teams typosquat AIDelivery High
Direct IOC hunt for the ommicrosoft.com typosquat domain referenced by Unit 42 in connection with Cloaked Ursa / Midnight Blizzard Teams credential-harvesting infrastructure. Sweeps Teams/Office activity, AAD sign-ins, DNS resolutions, and proxy traffic for any reference to the domain. Rationale: ommicrosoft.com is the only hard IOC in the article — a single-character typosquat of microsoft.com that Unit 42 ties to Cloaked Ursa Teams credential-harvesting. Any resolution, web request, sign-in reference, or Teams artifact mentioning this string is high-fidelity. Union covers chat, sign-in, DNS, and proxy surfaces because the same domain may surface across all four during the kill chain.
ATT&CKT1583.001 T1566.003 T1656
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution Web Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel platform / TIP fetching the IOC for analysis
  • Security researcher manually pivoting on the domain
  • Sandbox detonation submitting URL for analysis
  • Phishing-simulation vendor staging a lookalike for an awareness exercise
  • Mail security gateway sandbox following the link from a quarantined message
Suppression filter
| where SrcIP !in ("<SOC sandbox IP>","<TIP enrichment IP>")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the source — internal SOC tooling vs end-user host. If a Teams sender UPN or sign-in UPN contains the domain, treat as confirmed Cloaked Ursa attempted contact. 2) Contain: sinkhole / block ommicrosoft.com at the proxy and resolver tier, block the sender tenant in Teams external access, and (for any user with a sign-in attempt or click) revoke sessions and force credential rotation. Push an Entra ID Conditional Access policy blocking sign-ins where Resource or App matches the IOC. 3) Hunt: pivot on the resolved IP(s) over the last 90 days in DnsEvents / DeviceNetworkEvents and proxy logs; check UrlClickEvents for any click-through; review OfficeActivity for chat history from the sender tenant to enumerate additional victims.
let IOC = dynamic(["ommicrosoft.com"]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (DeviceNetworkEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where RemoteUrl has_any (IOC) or AdditionalFields has_any (IOC)
        | project Timestamp, Source="NetworkEvents", DeviceName, AccountUpn=InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP),
    (UrlClickEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where Url has_any (IOC)
        | project Timestamp, Source="UrlClickEvents", DeviceName="", AccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName="", RemoteUrl=Url, RemoteIP=tostring(IPAddress)),
    (CloudAppEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where Application =~ "Microsoft Teams"
        | extend Raw = tostring(RawEventData), Acts = tostring(ActivityObjects)
        | where Raw has_any (IOC) or Acts has_any (IOC)
        | project Timestamp, Source="Teams", DeviceName="", AccountUpn=AccountDisplayName, InitiatingProcessFileName=ActionType, RemoteUrl=ObjectName, RemoteIP=IPAddress),
    (AADSignInEventsBeta
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where AccountUpn has_any (IOC) or AlternateSignInName has_any (IOC) or ResourceDisplayName has_any (IOC)
        | project Timestamp, Source="AADSignIn", DeviceName=DeviceName, AccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName=Application, RemoteUrl=ResourceDisplayName, RemoteIP=IPAddress)
| order by Timestamp desc
let IOC = dynamic(["ommicrosoft.com"]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (OfficeActivity
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where UserId has_any (IOC) or tostring(Parameters) has_any (IOC)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="OfficeActivity", Operation, User=UserId, SrcIP=ClientIP, Detail=tostring(Parameters)),
    (SigninLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where UserPrincipalName has_any (IOC) or AppDisplayName has_any (IOC) or ResourceDisplayName has_any (IOC) or AlternateSignInName has_any (IOC)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="SigninLogs", Operation=OperationName, User=UserPrincipalName, SrcIP=IPAddress, Detail=strcat(AppDisplayName," | ",ResultDescription)),
    (DnsEvents
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where Name has_any (IOC)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="DnsEvents", Operation=QueryTypeName, User="", SrcIP=ClientIP, Detail=Name),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where DestinationHostName has_any (IOC) or RequestURL has_any (IOC) or DestinationDnsDomain has_any (IOC)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="Proxy/CSL", Operation=DeviceAction, User=SourceUserName, SrcIP=SourceIP, Detail=coalesce(RequestURL, DestinationHostName))
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Cloaked Ursa ommicrosoft.com Typosquat Domain Resolution

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",

         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |

    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:

    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer

author: Clankerusecase

Actions on Objectives
—
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Phar archive or PHPSpreadsheet RCE marker written by web-server process
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] PHPSpreadsheet phar:/// three-slash wrapper in HTTP request (CVE-2026-45034) · [LLM] Web-server process (php-fpm / apache / nginx / w3wp) spawning shell or network tooling · Article-specific behavioural hunt — [GHSA / CRITICAL] CVE-2026-45034: PHPSpreadsheet has a patch bypass for CVE-2026
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
PHPSpreadsheet phar:/// three-slash wrapper in HTTP request (CVE-2026-45034) AIExploitation High
Hunts inbound HTTP requests carrying the patch-bypass form 'phar:///path/file.phar/inner' (three or more slashes after the scheme) used to evade PHPSpreadsheet's File::prohibitWrappers helper. The single-slash form 'phar://x/' is correctly rejected by the patch; the triple-slash variant is the live bypass that still reaches PHP's phar stream wrapper. Rationale: Targets the literal bypass fingerprint from the advisory: 'phar:///path/file.phar/inner' with three or more slashes after the scheme. The advisory explicitly contrasts the rejected single-slash 'phar://x/dummy.csv' (negative control) against the surviving triple-slash 'phar:///work/exploit.phar/dummy.csv' (positive control), so a regex of `phar:/{3,}` plus its URL-encoded form is the exact patch-bypass discriminator. Defender XDR has no native inbound HTTP request telemetry so defender_kql is left empty; the detection lives in web-server / WAF logs that ship to Sentinel, Splunk Web, or Datadog. Did not perform external web search — the GitHub Security Advisory is itself the authoritative source for this CVE.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorised vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Acunetix, Qualys, Burp Suite Pro) probing for stream-wrapper / phar deserialization CVEs
  • Internal red-team / purple-team exercises replaying the GHSA-87m4-826x-3crx PoC against staging
  • Developer regression tests against patched releases verifying the negative control still hits
  • Security researcher traffic against public bug-bounty scope using phar:// payloads on unrelated apps
Suppression filter
// Suppress known scanner User-Agents in Sentinel
| where UserAgent !has_any ("Nessus", "Qualys", "Acunetix", "Nuclei", "Burp", "OWASP ZAP", "WhiteHat", "AppScan")
// Suppress allow-listed pentest source ranges (replace with your watchlist)
| where SourceIP !in ("203.0.113.0/24")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm the target endpoint hosts a PHPSpreadsheet-backed feature (file upload, XLSX/CSV import, report generator). Cross-check the source IP against scanner allow-lists; pull the full request body if WAF retains it and identify the 'file' / 'filename' / 'path' parameter that carried the phar:/// value. Capture the User-Agent and any session/auth context (was this authenticated?). Step 2 (contain): Block the source IP at the WAF/edge; if the target is PHP 7.x with PHPSpreadsheet <= 1.30.4, treat as confirmed RCE and isolate the web host from internal networks; snapshot for forensics. Apply the str_contains('://') fix or upgrade to the fixed PHPSpreadsheet tag. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the host running UC2 (PHP-FPM / Apache spawning shell or network tools within 60s of the request), UC3 (.phar files written by the web-server user to upload/temp dirs), outbound DNS/HTTP from the web process to non-CDN destinations, and new files in /tmp, /dev/shm, web-root cron, or .ssh/a
let bypass_pattern = @"(?i)phar:/{3,}|phar%3a%2f%2f%2f";
let wrapper_pattern = @"(?i)phar:/{2}|phar%3a%2f%2f";
(W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| extend FullUrl = strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery)
| where FullUrl matches regex wrapper_pattern
| extend IsBypassVariant = iff(FullUrl matches regex bypass_pattern, "yes", "no")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP = cIP, URL = FullUrl, UserAgent = csUserAgent, Method = csMethod, Status = scStatus, IsBypassVariant, LogSource = "W3CIISLog")
| union (CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL matches regex wrapper_pattern
| extend IsBypassVariant = iff(RequestURL matches regex bypass_pattern, "yes", "no")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, URL = RequestURL, UserAgent = RequestClientApplication, Method = RequestMethod, Status = tostring(EventOutcome), IsBypassVariant, LogSource = "CommonSecurityLog")
| where IsBypassVariant == "yes"   // 3+ slashes after scheme = patch bypass
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Web-server process (php-fpm / apache / nginx / w3wp) spawning shell or network tooling AIExploitation Medium
Hunts post-exploitation behaviour following CVE-2026-45034 RCE on PHP 7.x — the phar metadata __wakeup/__destruct gadget runs inside the web-server worker, so the parent of any spawned shell/network LOLBin is php-fpm, apache2, httpd, nginx, or w3wp.exe. Article-specific because PHP web workers almost never legitimately spawn sh/bash/curl/wget/nc. Rationale: The advisory states the gadget chain runs '__wakeup' and '__destruct' on PHP 7.x 'inside the victim process' — meaning the PHP web worker. So the post-RCE pivot is the same web-worker process spawning anything that's not another PHP worker. Excluding php→php parents (legitimate FPM pool spawning) and constraining child to shell/network LOLBins narrows the FP surface. Marked hunting (not alerting) because legitimate apps do shell out from PHP for image/video processing. Did not perform external web search — the technical detail in the GitHub advisory was sufficient to write this detection.
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.001 T1190 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • WordPress / Drupal plugins that legitimately exec ImageMagick (convert), ffmpeg, or pdftotext via shell
  • PHP-based CI/CD or deployment dashboards that shell out to git / rsync / ssh
  • Composer post-install hooks running in production with shell child processes
  • Monitoring / health-check PHP endpoints that exec system commands (df, uptime, ps)
  • Backup scripts triggered from web cron that invoke curl / wget to S3 / cloud storage
Suppression filter
// Defender — drop known-good wrappers
| where ProcessCommandLine !has_any ("/usr/bin/convert", "ImageMagick", "ffmpeg", "pdftotext", "/opt/app/healthcheck.sh")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "composer"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the parent PHP worker's recent request log (Apache/Nginx access log within 5 minutes of the child spawn) and look for 'phar://' or 'phar%3A%2F%2F' in any URL or POST body — that's the smoking gun tying this to UC1. Check the spawned child's cmdline for download URLs, reverse-shell signatures, or base64 blobs. Confirm whether the host runs PHP 7.x and PHPSpreadsheet <= 1.30.4 (1.x branch). Step 2 (contain): Kill the spawned child + parent worker, isolate the web host from internal networks, snapshot for forensics. Block any outbound IPs/domains the child contacted. Step 3 (hunt): Look for newly-written files in /tmp, /dev/shm, /var/tmp, web-root upload dirs, and ~/.ssh/. Pivot on the web user's account for new cron entries, systemd timers, or .bashrc modifications. Search the asset for .phar files (UC3) and check WAF for other phar:/// requests across the estate.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm","php-fpm.exe","php","php.exe","php-cgi.exe","apache2","httpd","httpd.exe","nginx","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","ksh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl","curl.exe","wget","wget.exe","nc","ncat","ncat.exe","socat","python","python3","python.exe","perl","ruby","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| where AccountName != "" and AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","php.exe","php","php-cgi.exe","apache2","httpd","nginx","w3wp.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat","python","python3","perl","ruby","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phar archive or PHPSpreadsheet RCE marker written by web-server process AIDelivery Medium
Hunts for .phar files written into web-server-writable directories by a PHP/web-worker process (staging step of CVE-2026-45034) and for the PoC artefact file 'pwned_marker' that the published exploit drops on successful RCE. .phar uploads to web roots are extremely unusual outside of deliberate deployment. Rationale: Two article-specific strings drive this: '.phar' (the exploit archive extension referenced throughout the advisory — exploit.phar in the PoC) and 'pwned_marker' (the literal file the published gadget writes containing 'WAKEUP: phpspreadsheet-bypass' / 'DESTRUCT: phpspreadsheet-bypass'). Both must be written by a web-worker process, which is the parent constraint that turns it from a generic 'phar file appeared' dashboard into a CVE-tied detection. Did not perform external web search — the advisory contained sufficient detail.
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Composer / Phar deployment where a build step writes packaged .phar archives into the webroot (rare in production but happens in dev environments)
  • Security team / internal red-team running the GHSA-87m4-826x-3crx run.sh reproducer against a lab
  • Static-analysis tooling that materialises phar test fixtures during CI runs that share a host with a webserver
  • Backup or update scripts that include phar files among the artefacts they restore into the web root
Suppression filter
// Defender — exclude known build / deploy paths
| where FolderPath !has_any ("/opt/build/", "/var/cache/composer/", "/tmp/composer-", "\\build\\artifacts\\")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "composer"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Hash the written file (SHA256) and check against threat-intel; correlate timestamp with the webserver access log to find the request that triggered the write — look specifically for 'phar://' or the IOFactory::load entry point in the application logs. Read the file content if 'pwned_marker' was found (the published PoC writes 'WAKEUP: phpspreadsheet-bypass' and 'DESTRUCT: phpspreadsheet-bypass'). Step 2 (contain): Quarantine the file, isolate the host, identify whether the asset is PHP 7.x with PHPSpreadsheet <= 1.30.4 (the only branch with RCE exposure). Reset any credentials that were resident in the web process environment. Step 3 (hunt): Look for other .phar artefacts across the estate written by web workers in the last 30 days; pivot on the writing-process command line for IOFactory::load patterns; check for the post-RCE shell-spawn (UC2) on the same host within ±5 minutes; review WAF for inbound 'phar://' requests (UC1) targeting the same endpoint.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm","php-fpm.exe","php","php.exe","php-cgi.exe","apache2","httpd","httpd.exe","nginx","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe")
| where FileName endswith ".phar"
     or FileName =~ "pwned_marker"
     or FileName =~ "exploit.phar"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, FileSize,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","php.exe","php","php-cgi","apache2","httpd","nginx","w3wp.exe")
| where TargetFileName endswith ".phar"
     or TargetFileName =~ "pwned_marker"
     or TargetFileName =~ "exploit.phar"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSize, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

AI brands as bait: How threat actors are using the AI hype in social engineering

Microsoft Security Blog
2026-06-08 17 use cases 7 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

As threat actors operationalize AI to accelerate attacks, they are also leveraging the wider global interest around AI itself as a social engineering lure. The post AI brands as bait: How threat actors are using the AI hype in social engineering appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

ChatGPT Plus payment-update phishing emails (display-name + subject lure) AIDelivery High
Detects the Microsoft-tracked ChatGPT-themed credential/credit-card phishing wave (4,500 emails to South Africa on 5 May 2026, peaking 100k/day across CH/AT/ZA) that impersonates OpenAI billing with the urgent 'update your payment method or downgrade' lure. Pivots on the verbatim sender display name and subject pattern the campaign uses. Rationale: Pulls the campaign's two strongest invariants: SenderDisplayName 'ChatGPT' and the verbatim Subject token 'ChatGPT Plus' co-occurring with the urgency-lure words ('payment method', 'continues to work', 'downgraded', 'free plan') quoted in the MSTI write-up. Excludes the real openai.com sending domain to drop legitimate billing.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1656
Data sourcesEmail
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security-awareness team forwarding a sample of the phish internally for training
  • Legitimate OpenAI dunning emails (caught by the openai.com sender-domain filter)
  • Customer-support reply chains that quote the original phish subject
  • Third-party billing aggregators that reuse the 'Plus subscription' phrasing
  • Newsletters/blog digests embedding the lure as a screenshot/text quote
Suppression filter
and SenderFromDomain !endswith "openai.com" and SenderFromDomain !endswith "stripe.com" and not (SenderFromAddress has_any ("phishtest","awareness","knowbe4"))
Response runbook
Triage: review SenderFromAddress, SenderIPv4, and UrlDomain on the matching EmailEvents row; confirm the URL chain does not terminate at openai.com or stripe.com. Contain: soft-delete and add the sender + URL domain to the org tenant block list via Defender for O365 Tenant Allow/Block list; trigger AIR investigation for in-mailbox copies. Hunt: pivot on UrlClickEvents over the past 30 days for the matching NetworkMessageId / UrlChain, then on DeviceProcessEvents for any process spawned within 60s of the click on affected hosts to spot credential-harvest follow-through.
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where (SenderDisplayName =~ "ChatGPT" or SenderFromAddress has "chatgpt")
    and Subject has "ChatGPT Plus"
    and Subject has_any ("payment method","continues to work","update your payment","downgraded","free plan")
| where SenderFromDomain !endswith "openai.com"
| join kind=leftouter (EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain) on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderDisplayName, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, Url, UrlDomain, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation
| order by Timestamp desc
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where OfficeWorkload =~ "Exchange"
| where Subject has "ChatGPT Plus" and Subject has_any ("payment method","continues to work","update your payment","downgraded","free plan")
| where tostring(P2Sender) !endswith "openai.com"
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ClientIP, Subject, Sender = tostring(P2Sender), Recipients = tostring(P2RecipientList), MessageId = tostring(InternetMessageId), Operation
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Claude 'Appeal Request' phishing email with PDF attachment lure AIDelivery High
Detects the Anthropic-impersonating phishing wave (20-22 Apr 2026, 2000+ orgs, primarily US/UK/IN tech sector) that uses the display names 'Anthropic Teams' / 'Anthropic PBC', a 'Claude Appeal Request' subject, and a 'Fill and Sign Claude Appeal Form.pdf' attachment carrying the AiTM credential-harvest link to dash.awaydouble[.]org. Rationale: Three article-specific high-fidelity tokens: the verbatim attachment FileName 'Fill and Sign Claude Appeal Form.pdf', the SenderDisplayName values 'Anthropic Teams' / 'Anthropic PBC', and the 'Claude Appeal Request' Subject. The PDF filename alone is essentially zero-FP. The display-name + subject combo is the fallback for renamed attachments. Anti-AiTM lure (dash.awaydouble[.]org) is covered separately in UC3.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1656 T1557
Data sourcesEmail
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal awareness team forwarding the captured sample as training material
  • Legitimate Anthropic trust-and-safety enforcement emails (filtered via anthropic.com domain)
  • Customer-support escalation threads quoting the lure subject
  • Legal/compliance teams forwarding the phish to internal counsel
  • Security-vendor breach-report digests embedding the lure as a screenshot
Suppression filter
and SenderFromDomain !endswith "anthropic.com" and not (SenderFromAddress has_any ("phishtest","awareness","knowbe4","@<your-soc-mailbox>"))
Response runbook
Triage: confirm SenderFromDomain is not anthropic.com and check whether the embedded PDF link resolves to dash.awaydouble[.]org or another non-Anthropic domain. Contain: soft-delete + zap all mailbox copies via Defender AIR; add the SenderFromAddress and IP to tenant block list; force token-revoke + password reset for any RecipientEmailAddress whose mailbox shows the message opened or attachment clicked. Hunt: query UrlClickEvents for clicks on dash.awaydouble[.]org / awaydouble[.]org over the past 60 days and SigninLogs for the same UPN for non-compliant-device or anomalous-country sign-ins in the click + 24h window — classic AiTM token-theft pattern.
let suspect_mail = EmailEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where SenderDisplayName in~ ("Anthropic Teams","Anthropic PBC")
         or Subject matches regex @"(?i)Claude\s+Appeal\s+Request"
    | where SenderFromDomain !endswith "anthropic.com";
let suspect_attach = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileType =~ "pdf"
    | where FileName =~ "Fill and Sign Claude Appeal Form.pdf"
         or FileName matches regex @"(?i)(Claude|Anthropic).{0,20}Appeal.{0,20}Form.*\.pdf$";
suspect_mail
| join kind=inner suspect_attach on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderDisplayName, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, FileName, FileSize, SHA256, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation
| order by Timestamp desc
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where OfficeWorkload =~ "Exchange"
| where Subject matches regex @"(?i)Claude\s+Appeal\s+Request"
    or tostring(ItemAttachments) has "Fill and Sign Claude Appeal Form.pdf"
| where tostring(P2Sender) !endswith "anthropic.com"
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ClientIP, Subject, Sender = tostring(P2Sender), Recipients = tostring(P2RecipientList), Attachments = tostring(ItemAttachments), MessageId = tostring(InternetMessageId)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Connection to AI-brand phishing / installer C2 infrastructure (MSTI June 2026 IOCs) AICommand & Control High
Network-side detection for the eight Microsoft-published domains backing the ChatGPT/Claude AiTM landing pages and the fake DeepSeek/Manus/Seedance installer C2. Fires on any DNS resolution or HTTP egress to the IOC set; high-fidelity because these are dedicated attacker infrastructure with no known legitimate use. Rationale: Eight domains explicitly attributed by Microsoft Threat Intelligence to this campaign: legendarytrendsbay.shop (ChatGPT phish landing), dash.awaydouble.org / awaydouble.org (Claude AiTM landing), and the four installer-C2 domains. Detection is a literal IOC match — appropriate for alerting tier because attribution is high-confidence and the domains have no legitimate business use.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SOC analyst manually visiting the IOC for triage (filter on known-analyst workstations)
  • Sandbox / detonation chamber egress to the IOCs during sample analysis
  • Threat-intel scanner (Recorded Future, VirusTotal Hunting) crawling the IOC
  • Browser prefetch / DoH safety check resolving the domain without a real visit
  • Email security product following the redirect chain for verdict determination (e.g. Defender Safe Links scan)
Suppression filter
and InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("<known-analyst-account>") and DeviceName !in~ ("<sandbox-host-list>")
Response runbook
Triage: identify the InitiatingProcessFileName (browser vs LOLBin vs unknown installer) on the affected DeviceName and whether the URL path contained /ChatGPT/ (phish lure) or pointed at a binary payload. Contain: block the eight domains at perimeter DNS/proxy AND in Defender Indicators; isolate the device via Defender LiveResponse if the calling process was anything other than a browser visiting the phish landing. Hunt: pivot DeviceProcessEvents for the same DeviceId across the past 14 days for any of the lure executables (deepseek-v4-*_x64.exe etc.) and for SigninLogs MFA-challenge / anomalous-token events on the logged-on user post-visit (AiTM token theft).
let ioc_domains = dynamic(["legendarytrendsbay.shop","dash.awaydouble.org","awaydouble.org","servicing.pureplantcravings.com","pureplantcravings.com","brokeapt.com","pan.ssffaa19.xyz","ssffaa19.xyz"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend host = tolower(tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl).Host))
| where host in (ioc_domains)
    or RemoteUrl has_any (ioc_domains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, host, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
let ioc_domains = dynamic(["legendarytrendsbay.shop","dash.awaydouble.org","awaydouble.org","servicing.pureplantcravings.com","pureplantcravings.com","brokeapt.com","pan.ssffaa19.xyz","ssffaa19.xyz"]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (ImDnsActivity
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
        | where tolower(DnsQuery) in (ioc_domains) or DnsQuery has_any (ioc_domains)
        | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Indicator = DnsQuery, EventVendor, EventProduct, EventKind = "dns"),
    (ImWebSession
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
        | where Url has_any (ioc_domains) or DstHostname in (ioc_domains)
        | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Indicator = coalesce(DstHostname, Url), EventVendor, EventProduct, EventKind = "web"),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
        | where DestinationHostName has_any (ioc_domains) or RequestURL has_any (ioc_domains)
        | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname = SourceHostName, SrcIpAddr = SourceIP, SrcUsername = SourceUserName, Indicator = coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), EventVendor = DeviceVendor, EventProduct = DeviceProduct, EventKind = "firewall")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Network Connection to AI-Brand Phishing IOC Domains (MSTI Jun 2026)
id: 2d4a9b6e-3c2d-4f7a-b8e1-7a0c1e9d4f55
description: Detects DNS or HTTP egress to the eight Microsoft Threat Intelligence-published domains backing the ChatGPT/Claude AiTM landing pages and fake AI installer C2.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/08/ai-brands-as-bait-how-threat-actors-are-using-the-ai-hype-in-social-engineering/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/09
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1568
logsource:
  category: dns
detection:
  selection:
    query:
      - 'legendarytrendsbay.shop'
      - 'dash.awaydouble.org'
      - 'awaydouble.org'
      - 'servicing.pureplantcravings.com'
      - 'pureplantcravings.com'
      - 'brokeapt.com'
      - 'pan.ssffaa19.xyz'
      - 'ssffaa19.xyz'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Threat-intel scanning / sandbox detonation from SOC infrastructure
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon AND @EventID:(3 OR 22) AND (@DestinationHostname:(legendarytrendsbay.shop OR dash.awaydouble.org OR awaydouble.org OR servicing.pureplantcravings.com OR pureplantcravings.com OR brokeapt.com OR pan.ssffaa19.xyz OR ssffaa19.xyz) OR @QueryName:(legendarytrendsbay.shop OR dash.awaydouble.org OR awaydouble.org OR servicing.pureplantcravings.com OR pureplantcravings.com OR brokeapt.com OR pan.ssffaa19.xyz OR ssffaa19.xyz))) OR (source:(zscaler OR paloalto OR fortinet OR cisco_umbrella) AND @url:(*legendarytrendsbay.shop* OR *awaydouble.org* OR *pureplantcravings.com* OR *brokeapt.com* OR *ssffaa19.xyz*))
(#event_simpleName=DnsRequest OR #event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 OR #event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP6)
| DomainName=/^(legendarytrendsbay\.shop|dash\.awaydouble\.org|awaydouble\.org|servicing\.pureplantcravings\.com|pureplantcravings\.com|brokeapt\.com|pan\.ssffaa19\.xyz|ssffaa19\.xyz)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
| sort(_count, order=desc)
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.src) as src values(All_Traffic.dest_ip) as dest_ip from datamodel=Network_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest IN ("legendarytrendsbay.shop","dash.awaydouble.org","awaydouble.org","servicing.pureplantcravings.com","pureplantcravings.com","brokeapt.com","pan.ssffaa19.xyz","ssffaa19.xyz")) by All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

Execution or drop of fake AI-platform installer (DeepSeek/Manus/Seedance/GPT-5.5/Kimi) AIInstallation High
Detects the malicious installer binaries Storm-3075 ships through SEO-poisoned GitHub repos masquerading as AI tools (DeepSeek-V4, Manus AI, Seedance, GPT-5.5, Kimi-Swarm). Combines verbatim filename match, the eight MSTI-published SHA256 hashes, and a permissive regex pattern keyed on the consistent '*_x64.exe' naming convention dropped into Downloads/Temp. Rationale: Three layers of fidelity: (1) verbatim FileName match for the seven binaries enumerated in MSTI's lure-table (rows 2-6); (2) hash-equal on all eight published SHA256 IOCs — zero-FP even if the file is renamed; (3) regex on the campaign's consistent '*_x64.exe' naming convention scoped to Downloads/Temp/Public to catch future siblings dropped from the same MSaaS signing pipeline. Article explicitly notes Storm-3075 uses these names through fake GitHub orgs (DeepSeek-V4, ManusAI-agent, bytedance-seedance).
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1608.005 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate DeepSeek / ByteDance Seedance / Moonshot Kimi installer downloaded from the official vendor site (distinguishable via publisher cert: vendor-signed not MSaaS-signed)
  • Security researcher detonating samples in a corp-attached sandbox VM
  • IT redistributing the genuine open-source AI model launcher to dev workstations
  • Renamed in-house tool that accidentally matches the naming regex (e.g. 'kimi-swarm-station' if your firm runs an internal swarm orchestrator)
  • Threat-hunting team replaying historical IOCs as part of detection-engineering validation
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("msiexec.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("\\\\<dfs-share>\\\\Software\\\\")) and DeviceName !in~ ("<sandbox-host-list>")
Response runbook
Triage: pull SHA256 + publisher cert details for the matching ProcessId; if hash is on the MSTI list, treat as confirmed Storm-3075. Check ParentImage — Downloads-folder browser parent confirms SEO-poisoning vector; cmd/PowerShell parent suggests script-stage. Contain: isolate the host via Defender LiveResponse, kill the process, hash-block the SHA256 tenant-wide in Defender Indicators, revoke the user's Azure AD refresh tokens. Hunt: look for the same SHA256 / FileName across the whole estate (DeviceFileEvents), pivot DeviceNetworkEvents on the affected host to the IOC domains in UC3 for the past 30 days, and review the user's browser history / EmailUrlInfo for the GitHub-repo SEO landing.
let lure_binaries = dynamic(["deepseek-v4-pro_x64.exe","deepseek-v4-flash_x64.exe","Manus_AI_Desktop_x64.exe","seedance_x64.exe","gpt-5.5-Pro_x64.exe","gpt-5.5-Thinking_x64.exe","Kimi-Swarm-Station_x64.exe"]);
let ioc_sha256 = dynamic(["791efb555eefb7215e96659a1353a97416743b66bdd72705493129c64057d40e","c7c5072df9f83f4c440a5c3bb4be1d5f6c67bbf78f196406ca20d27b43b975b8","0a26238f6c516de5885457c93042531aa59bc206a9537cebf5267cedc6c68531","8610d4fb0ec5b525071c2aaec4df0f8fcbb3673aba58a7e1959fc44e83c0e2ca","99231deb373997364381d1eb513d2d42231d418c3a2db9007c5af9bd56ab9371","25270cc429ada8028b5b33220ed412c47907ecceea7377d608fac5af01bed56a","56d722b0331bf0aaa86bb37483486c6dff6ad9427fc473ed7c3226c21a9bdd23","5455341ed1bbe75a664fca2dd0794c508e1874f75360253a7ff5bc119bc92d80"]);
let ai_lure_regex = @"(?i)^(deepseek-v\d+(-pro|-flash)?|manus_ai_desktop|seedance|gpt-\d+(\.\d+)?-(pro|thinking)|kimi-swarm-station)_x64\.exe$";
union isfuzzy=false
    (DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
        | where FileName in~ (lure_binaries)
            or SHA256 in (ioc_sha256)
            or (FileName matches regex ai_lure_regex and FolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\",@"\Temp\",@"\AppData\Local\Temp\",@"\Public\"))
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, EvtKind = "process", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
    (DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
        | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
        | where FileName in~ (lure_binaries) or SHA256 in (ioc_sha256)
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, EvtKind = "file", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessParentFileName)
| order by Timestamp desc

let ioc_sha256 = dynamic(["791efb555eefb7215e96659a1353a97416743b66bdd72705493129c64057d40e","c7c5072df9f83f4c440a5c3bb4be1d5f6c67bbf78f196406ca20d27b43b975b8","0a26238f6c516de5885457c93042531aa59bc206a9537cebf5267cedc6c68531","8610d4fb0ec5b525071c2aaec4df0f8fcbb3673aba58a7e1959fc44e83c0e2ca","99231deb373997364381d1eb513d2d42231d418c3a2db9007c5af9bd56ab9371","25270cc429ada8028b5b33220ed412c47907ecceea7377d608fac5af01bed56a","56d722b0331bf0aaa86bb37483486c6dff6ad9427fc473ed7c3226c21a9bdd23","5455341ed1bbe75a664fca2dd0794c508e1874f75360253a7ff5bc119bc92d80"]);
let ai_lure_regex = @"(?i)(deepseek-v\d+(-pro|-flash)?|manus_ai_desktop|seedance|gpt-\d+(\.\d+)?-(pro|thinking)|kimi-swarm-station)_x64\.exe";
union isfuzzy=true
    (ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
        | where tolower(ActingProcessName) has_any (lure_binaries)
            or SHA256 in (ioc_sha256)
            or ActingProcessName matches regex ai_lure_regex
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EvtKind="process", ActingProcessName, ParentProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256),

| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.process_path) as path from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("deepseek-v4-pro_x64.exe","deepseek-v4-flash_x64.exe","Manus_AI_Desktop_x64.exe","seedance_x64.exe","gpt-5.5-Pro_x64.exe","gpt-5.5-Thinking_x64.exe","Kimi-Swarm-Station_x64.exe") OR Processes.process_hash IN ("791efb555eefb7215e96659a1353a97416743b66bdd72705493129c64057d40e","c7c5072df9f83f4c440a5c3bb4be1d5f6c67bbf78f196406ca20d27b43b975b8","0a26238f6c516de5885457c93042531aa59bc206a9537cebf5267cedc6c68531","8610d4fb0ec5b525071c2aaec4df0f8fcbb3673aba58a7e1959fc44e83c0e2ca","99231deb373997364381d1eb513d2d42231d418c3a2db9007c5af9bd56ab9371","25270cc429ada8028b5b33220ed412c47907ecceea7377d608fac5af01bed56a","56d722b0331bf0aaa86bb37483486c6dff6ad9427fc473ed7c3226c21a9bdd23","5455341ed1bbe75a664fca2dd0794c508e1874f75360253a7ff5bc119bc92d80")) by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.process_path) as path from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("deepseek-v4-pro_x64.exe","deepseek-v4-flash_x64.exe","Manus_AI_Desktop_x64.exe","seedance_x64.exe","gpt-5.5-Pro_x64.exe","gpt-5.5-Thinking_x64.exe","Kimi-Swarm-Station_x64.exe") OR Processes.process_hash IN ("791efb555eefb7215e96659a1353a97416743b66bdd72705493129c64057d40e","c7c5072df9f83f4c440a5c3bb4be1d5f6c67bbf78f196406ca20d27b43b975b8","0a26238f6c516de5885457c93042531aa59bc206a9537cebf5267cedc6c68531","8610d4fb0ec5b525071c2aaec4df0f8fcbb3673aba58a7e1959fc44e83c0e2ca","99231deb373997364381d1eb513d2d42231d418c3a2db9007c5af9bd56ab9371","25270cc429ada8028b5b33220ed412c47907ecceea7377d608fac5af01bed56a","56d722b0331bf0aaa86bb37483486c6dff6ad9427fc473ed7c3226c21a9bdd23","5455341ed1bbe75a664fca2dd0794c508e1874f75360253a7ff5bc119bc92d80")) by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
Phishing redirect chain via awstrack.me / Rebrandly into AI-themed landing path AIDelivery Medium
Detects user clicks on the multi-hop redirect chain Storm-3075/affiliates use to launder phish URLs: legit CRM (bitrix24) → Amazon awstrack.me email-tracking → Rebrandly short link → compromised legendarytrendsbay[.]shop /ChatGPT/ path (or sibling AI-themed paths). Targets the SHAPE of the chain (awstrack.me forwarding into an AI-brand path), not just static IOCs, so it also catches campaign rotation. Rationale: Two pivot shapes from the MSTI ChatGPT-phish attack chain: (1) literal IOC match on the six known phish landings; (2) behavioural pattern of a click through awstrack.me/Rebrandly/bitrix24 that terminates at a path containing an AI-brand token — this is the exact funnel diagrammed in Figure 1 and survives URL rotation since the AI-brand path component is the lure invariant. Path-regex /(ChatGPT|Claude|Anthropic|DeepSeek)/ also catches the article's note that the threat actor placed phishing pages in a /ChatGPT/ folder on compromised legendarytrendsbay[.]shop.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1102 T1656
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Marketing or sales team using Bitrix24 CRM legitimately, with AWS SES tracking and an AI-themed campaign name in the URL
  • Legitimate Anthropic / OpenAI newsletter using Rebrandly short links (verify the terminal landing is the genuine vendor domain)
  • Security awareness training that simulates this exact lure (Defender Attack Simulator may surface here)
  • Procurement team evaluating an AI vendor demo via a shortened URL containing the vendor name
  • Internal employee blog post embedding a Rebrandly link that references an AI tool
Suppression filter
and AccountUpn !in~ ("<known-marketing-accounts>") and not (UrlChain has "openai.com" or UrlChain has "anthropic.com" or UrlChain has "deepseek.com")
Response runbook
Triage: inspect the full UrlChain field — confirm the chain terminates at a non-vendor domain (legendarytrendsbay[.]shop, awaydouble[.]org, etc.) not openai.com / anthropic.com / deepseek.com. Pull EmailUrlInfo by the matching NetworkMessageId to identify the originating phish. Contain: revoke active sessions for the AccountUpn via Entra ID risky-user workflow; add Conditional Access requirement for re-MFA on next sign-in; block the terminal landing domain at proxy. Hunt: SigninLogs for the same UPN looking for unfamiliar-location or device-not-compliant sign-ins in the click + 4h window (AiTM token theft); EmailEvents for siblings of the same campaign that hit other recipients.
let phish_landings = dynamic(["legendarytrendsbay.shop","dash.awaydouble.org","awaydouble.org","servicing.pureplantcravings.com","pureplantcravings.com","brokeapt.com"]);
UrlClickEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
| where Url has_any (phish_landings)
    or UrlChain has_any (phish_landings)
    or (Url has_any ("awstrack.me","rebrand.ly","rebrandly.com","bitrix24.com") and Url matches regex @"(?i)(chatgpt|claude|anthropic|deepseek|manus|seedance|gpt-?5|kimi)")
    or Url matches regex @"(?i)https?://[^/]+/(ChatGPT|Claude|Anthropic|DeepSeek)/"
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlChain, ActionType, IsClickedThrough, IPAddress, Workload
| order by Timestamp desc
let phish_landings = dynamic(["legendarytrendsbay.shop","dash.awaydouble.org","awaydouble.org","servicing.pureplantcravings.com","pureplantcravings.com","brokeapt.com"]);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where Url has_any (phish_landings)
    or (Url has_any ("awstrack.me","rebrand.ly","rebrandly.com","bitrix24.com") and Url matches regex @"(?i)(chatgpt|claude|anthropic|deepseek|manus|seedance|gpt-?5|kimi)")
    or Url matches regex @"(?i)https?://[^/]+/(ChatGPT|Claude|Anthropic|DeepSeek)/"

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"

| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port

| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
